import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Ben Green's Open Problem 46

What is the largest $y$ for which one may cover the interval $[y]$ by residue classes $a_p \pmod{p}$, one for each prime $p \leq x$?

*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's Open Problem 46](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.46)
- [FGK18] Ford, K., Green, B., Konyagin, S., Maynard, J., & Tao, T. (2018). Long gaps between primes.
  Journal of the American Mathematical Society, 31(1), 65-105.
- [Iw78] Iwaniec, Henryk. "On the problem of Jacobsthal." Demonstratio Mathematica 11.1 (1978): 225-232.
-/

namespace Green46

open Filter
open scoped Asymptotics

/-- Given $x$ and $y$, can we cover the interval $[1, y]$ by residue classes $a_p \pmod p$
for each prime $p \le x$? -/
def IsCoveredByResidues (x y : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a : ℕ → ℕ, ∀ m ∈ Finset.Icc 1 y, ∃ p ≤ x, p.Prime ∧ m ≡ a p [MOD p]

/-- The maximum $y$ for a given $x$, cast to a real number for asymptotics. -/
noncomputable def maxY (x : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ((sSup { y | IsCoveredByResidues x y } : ℕ) : ℝ)

/-- Best-known lower bound [Ra38]. -/
noncomputable def bestLower (x : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  (x : ℝ) * Real.log (x : ℝ) * Real.log (Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ))) / Real.log (Real.log (x : ℝ))

/-- Best-known upper bound [Iw78]. -/
noncomputable def bestUpper (x : ℕ) : ℝ := (x : ℝ) ^ 2

/-- We conjecture that the best-known lower bound can be improved. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_46.improve_lower :
    let ans := (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
    (bestLower =o[atTop] ans) ∧ (ans ≪ maxY) := by
  sorry

/-- We conjecture that the best-known upper bound can be improved. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_46.improve_upper :
    let ans := (answer(sorry) : ℕ → ℝ)
    (ans =o[atTop] bestUpper) ∧ (maxY ≪ ans) := by
  sorry

/-- It seems very likely that we must have $y \ll x^{1+o(1)}$ [Gr24]. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_46.improve_upper_conjectured :
    ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, (o =o[atTop] fun _ : ℕ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
      maxY ≪ fun x ↦ (x : ℝ) ^ (1 + o x) := by
  sorry

/-- Best known lower bound: $y \gg x \frac{\log x \log \log \log x}{\log \log x}$ [Ra38]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem green_46.variants.lower :
    bestLower ≪ maxY := by
  sorry

/-- Best known upper bound: $y \ll x^2$ [Iw78]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem green_46.variants.upper :
    maxY ≪ bestUpper := by
  sorry

-- TODO(jeangud) Add similar problem mentioned in [Gr24, Problem 46]

end Green46

findings.description: The docstring attributes this bound to `[Ra38]`, but the definition is the stronger Ford–Green–Konyagin–Maynard–Tao bound, not Rankin's 1938 bound. The mathematical definition is correct.
findings.source_evidence: Green's Problem 46 attributes y ≫ x log x log log log x / log log x to reference [121], Long gaps between primes (2018). Section 1.1 of that paper explicitly distinguishes its bound Y(x) ≫ x log x log₃ x / log₂ x from Rankin's bound with denominator (log₂ x)². Sources: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.46 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5029.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `[Ra38]` in this docstring with the existing reference `[FGK18]`; leave the formula unchanged.

findings.description: The theorem's docstring repeats the incorrect `[Ra38]` attribution. Its displayed formula and Lean statement correctly give the newer bound, so this is a reference error rather than a mathematical misformalization.
findings.source_evidence: Green's Problem 46 cites Ford–Green–Konyagin–Maynard–Tao for this lower bound. Their paper, Section 1.1, states Y(x) ≫ x log x log₃ x / log₂ x and says it improves Rankin's bound with denominator (log₂ x)². Sources: https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.46 and https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.5029.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `[Ra38]` with `[FGK18]` in the theorem docstring. Keep the theorem statement and solved category.

reformulations.difference: The source uses the largest coverable integer; Lean takes a natural-number supremum and then casts it to ℝ.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For each x, zero is coverable. Every coverable y is strictly less than P(x), the product of primes at most x: CRT supplies k < P(x) with k ≡ a_p modulo every such prime, so k+1 cannot belong to any chosen class. Thus the set is nonempty and bounded, its natural supremum is attained, and no unbounded-set default value is reached. The scratch file proves attainment and IsCoveredByResidues x y ↔ (y : ℝ) ≤ maxY x.

reformulations.difference: The lower-bound improvement is requested through an auxiliary real-valued answer function satisfying a little-o/Big-O sandwich.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Existence of ans with bestLower =o ans and ans =O maxY is equivalent to bestLower =o maxY: use transitivity in one direction and choose ans = maxY in the other. This expresses improvement by a factor tending to infinity. Allowing signed functions does not change existence of a bound, since replacing ans by |ans| preserves both constraints. Both equivalences were checked in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The upper-bound improvement is requested through an auxiliary real-valued answer function rather than directly asserting maxY =o (x ↦ x²).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Existence of ans with ans =o bestUpper and maxY =O ans is equivalent to maxY =o bestUpper, by transitivity and, conversely, choosing ans = maxY. Replacing ans by |ans| preserves both constraints, so signed answer functions do not weaken the existence question. These equivalences were proved in Lean.

review.notes: All four definitions and five theorems were checked. No substantive mathematical misformalization was found; the findings are two occurrences of the same minor attribution error. The scratch file /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors and without using the problem's sorry-backed theorems. It proves supremum validity, equivalence to a finite decidable covering predicate, maxY(0)=maxY(1)=0, maxY(2)=1, maxY(3)=3, eventual positivity of the bounds, nontriviality of the answer constraints, and equivalence of o =o 1 with convergence to zero. Exhaustive finite tests also confirm the covering thresholds for x=4,5,7. The original Iwaniec article could not be retrieved because the publisher returned a bot challenge; the precise x² upper bound is nevertheless explicitly confirmed by both Green's comments and Section 1.1 of the cited later paper. The recorded open/solved categories agree with the consulted source.
